title: U.S. House · Oregon's 5th District
area: Central Oregon (Bend, Redmond) and outer-east Portland suburbs in Clackamas County (Happy Valley, Damascus, Estacada).

context.text: Incumbent Janelle Bynum defeated Zeva Rosenbaum 82.0%-17.4% in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. Patti Adair defeated Jonathan Lockwood 59.6%-39.7% in the Republican primary; Adair also won the Libertarian ballot line. Andrea Townsend is the Pacific Green Party nominee.

summary.text: Janelle Bynum is the Democratic nominee for re-election to Oregon's 5th Congressional District, which she has represented since January 2025. An electrical engineer and MBA who became a McDonald's franchise owner in Clackamas County, she served eight years in the Oregon House of Representatives, including as chair of the Committee on Small Business and Economic Development. In Congress she serves on the Financial Services Committee.

background.text: Born in 1975 and grew up in Washington, D.C., where she attended Banneker High School and graduated from The Madeira School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Florida A&M University (1996) and an MBA from the University of Michigan's Ross School of Business (2000).
Worked as an engineer, including as a steering systems engineer at General Motors; in 2002 she moved to Clackamas County, Oregon, to help run a McDonald's franchise and became a franchise owner.

Won an Oregon House seat (District 51) in 2016, defeating Republican Lori Chavez-DeRemer, then the mayor of Happy Valley, and was re-elected in 2018, 2020 and 2022 (District 39 after redistricting); served eight years, 2017 to 2025.

In the Oregon House, chaired the Committee on Small Business and Economic Development; her office says she led efforts that added $43 billion and over 6,000 jobs to Oregon's economy. She was chief sponsor of the 2023 Oregon CHIPS Act, a $210 million semiconductor industry initiative.
Elected to Congress on November 5, 2024, defeating incumbent Republican Lori Chavez-DeRemer; sworn in January 2025.

Serves on the House Financial Services Committee (Subcommittees on Housing and Insurance and on Capital Markets, and the Task Force on Monetary Policy, Treasury Market Resilience, and Economic Prosperity) and is a member of caucuses including the Congressional Black Caucus, Labor Caucus and Extreme Heat Caucus.
Has volunteered with the Ronald McDonald House Charities of Oregon board, Business Oregon, the Center for Women's Leadership, and the Oregon Commission on Black Affairs.
According to her office, she is the daughter of teachers and a mother of four who lives in Happy Valley with her husband Mark.

priorities.text: Says she is focused on creating good-paying jobs, strengthening public education, addressing the wildfire crisis, and lowering the cost of health care, prescription drugs and housing for working families.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Financial Services.

summary.text: Patti Adair is the Republican and Libertarian nominee for Oregon's 5th Congressional District. A certified public accountant and former Moss Adams auditor, she has served on the Deschutes County Commission since 2019 and previously chaired the county Republican Party. She won the May 2026 Republican primary and, according to her campaign, is running on fiscal responsibility, public safety, veterans and small businesses.

background.text: Born in Pendleton, Oregon, and raised on her family's ranch in Heppner, where she was a 4-H member; according to her campaign, her family settled in Eastern Oregon in 1884.
Attended the University of Oregon and later earned her CPA license from Central Washington University.
Worked as an auditor and full-cycle accountant at Moss Adams, and had a career in California before returning to Oregon in 2014 and settling in Sisters.
Is a former chair of the Deschutes County Republican Party.
Elected to the Deschutes County Commission in 2018 and re-elected in 2022; took office in 2019. According to her campaign, she oversees more than 1,200 employees and twenty-two departments.

Chairs the Central Oregon Commission on Transportation, serves as the Deschutes County Fair Association liaison and on the Local Government Advisory Committee, and, per her campaign, sits on 12 additional boards.
Describes the county's veterans village program and saving Worrell Wayside Park in Bend as her proudest accomplishments as commissioner.
Defeated Jonathan Lockwood in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary. According to her campaign, she is married to Bob, a retired surgeon, and lives on a horse ranch in Sisters.

priorities.text: Fiscal responsibility and oversight of tax dollars, drawing on her accounting background.
Public safety, citing her record as county commissioner on what she describes as fighting for safer communities.
Support for veterans, citing the county's veterans village program launched during her tenure as commissioner.

record.text: As Deschutes County Commissioner, has overseen the county's veterans village program and chairs the Central Oregon Commission on Transportation.

candidates.name: Andrea Townsend

summary.text: Andrea Townsend is the Pacific Green Party nominee for Oregon's 5th Congressional District; she was also the Pacific Green nominee for the seat in 2024.

background.text: Was the Pacific Green Party nominee for Oregon's 5th District in the November 2024 general election, receiving 6,193 votes; she is again the party's nominee in 2026.
